R1.keyFinding: Exposed monolithic oven_heating_system problem; bake/broil initially platform_implementation on Copernicus ACU relay path

R2.keyFinding: Independently confirmed bake/broil/convection as distinct testable heating functions; strengthened temperature_sensor and convection_fan

R3.keyFinding: Surface-control implementation changes (infinite switch vs ACU relay) while control_board → surface_heating_system invariant survives

R4.keyFinding: 7/7 boundary probes confirmed on PDF-grounded Samsung NE58 evidence; Samsung hardware names remain platform vocabulary

conceptRecommendations.freezeRationale: Mains supply prerequisite independently tested on all four manuals (Copernicus ACU power, LG no-power, LCX terminal block, Samsung SMPS/240 VAC). Distinct from control orchestration.

Control orchestration recurs across ACU, LG Main PCB, LCX control board, and Samsung Main/Sub PCB relay paths. Implementation names (ACU, sub PCB, relay bank) stay platform — functional control_board node holds.
Touch/keypad/HMI diagnostic domain distinct from control PCB on all four families (F2E1, F-1, -SE-, etc.).

R1 deferred pending cross-manufacturer evidence. R2–R4 each provide dedicated oven RTD procedures with independent failure routing (F-3/F3E0, E-21/E-22). Cavity temperature feedback earns canonical status.

R1 posed the question; R2 LG proved separate bake/broil/convection element tests. R3 LCX and R4 Samsung list distinct element rows/procedures. Monolithic aggregate has no independent diagnostic meaning — heat generation is a functional domain with instance-scoped functions, not one opaque node.

Dedicated bake procedure on LG, LCX, and Samsung; R1 Copernicus treated bake as relay-mediated platform test but did not contradict separate diagnostic function. Freeze as instance scope under oven heat generation domain — NOT a separate canonical component type.
Same evidence posture as bake — independent broil test on R2/R3/R4. Instance scope under oven heat generation domain.

Strong instance-scoped evidence on LG R2 and Samsung R4 electric convection element procedures. R3 LCX has no convection element proc; R1 deferred (gas convection path on Copernicus). Encode as INSTANCE_SCOPE when platform manual evidences electric convection element test — not unconditional canonical component.
conceptRecommendations.conditionalRule: Include in instanceScopes[] when procedure evidence exists for electric convection element; omit on platforms without dedicated convection heat path.

conceptRecommendations.freezeRationale: R3 infinite-switch and R4 radiant cooktop both test surface heat as a functional domain. R2 per-zone element procedures show overlay granularity (LF/LR/RR/RF/CR) without requiring per-zone canonical nodes. Functional domain: cooktop heat generation.

R3 falsified surface_control as canonical — infinite switch is LCX implementation. R4 Samsung knob/infinite-switch same posture. R1 ACU relay and R2 cook-top relay PCB are platform switching paths. Functional invariant: control_board → surface_heating_system. Do NOT promote infinite_switch, relay PCB, or sub PCB relay to canonical.
Physical radiant/bridge/ceran elements are platform instances under surface_heating_system. LG per-zone Ω procedures are overlay scope when OEM provides zone tests — not canonical component types.

LG R2 and Samsung R4 provide dedicated convection fan motor tests separate from heating elements. R1 combined vent/convection fan procedure creates ambiguity. R3 LCX documents fan behavior without fan procedure seed. Canonical only when platform procedure evidence distinguishes convection air circulation actuator — not unconditional on all electric ranges.

No manual in R1–R4 provides a dedicated electronics cooling fan procedure distinct from convection fan. R1 vent/convection combination insufficient to split. Revisit only if future manual evidences separate cooling vs convection diagnostic paths.

Protection behavior is real but implementation paths diverge: dedicated thermal-fuse proc (R1), F-6/F6E1 sensor route (R2/R3), thermostat continuity + E-08 (R4). Model as conditional/platform vocabulary (fuse vs hi-limit vs sensor-limited path) — analogous to refrigerator conditional concepts. Do NOT freeze a single thermal_protection canonical component.

Door authorization function recurs (LG standalone door switch, Samsung plunger switch, LCX latch-embedded logic). Functional door-state role holds; test packaging varies by platform. Conditional canonical — include when OEM provides distinct door-switch vs latch-actuator procedures.
Self-clean latch motor/micro-switch implementations on all four families. Actuator is platform knowledge; door authorization function may be CONDITIONAL via oven_door_switch when separately tested.
Cavity referenced in safety/operation text only — no standalone cavity diagnostic procedure on any manual in corpus.
Oven lamp procedures exist on LG and Samsung as accessory tests — not core electric range functional ontology. Platform overlay only.
Optional feature domain — LG warming drawer sensor/element on select models only. Insufficient cross-manufacturer evidence for rev1 canonical inclusion.
